.agent/W2-technical-design-cold.md:112:**Time and state.** Fixed 1-minute UTC step; all updates use exact rationals/decimal text and a defined end-of-step publication order. State: chamber air temperature `T` degC, controller demand, compressor `OFF|STARTING|RUNNING|FAILED`, grid/backup bus energized flags, generator `STOPPED|STARTING|RUNNING|FAILED`, transfer position `GRID|BACKUP|OPEN`, door `OPEN|CLOSED`, probe `OK|FAILED`. Private forcing: ambient `Ta`, door schedule, grid loss, generator failure, probe failure; private truth never serializes into a product envelope. Initial `T=3°C`, `Ta=20°C`, door closed, compressor off, grid and bus on, generator stopped, transfer grid, probe OK. Per minute, `heat_kWh = (heat_leak_kW_per_C*(Ta-T) + door_open*door_heat_kWh*60)*1/60`; `cool_kWh = compressor_running_and_bus_powered*cooling_kW*1/60`; `T_next=T+(heat_kWh-cool_kWh)/thermal_capacity_kWh_per_C`. Defaults: thermal capacity `1.2 kWh/degC`, leak `0.08 kW/degC`, door heat `0.02 kWh/min` (stored as `1.2 kW` equivalent while open), cooling `3 kW`, compressor start delay 1 minute, generator start delay 2 minutes, transfer delay 1 minute, start timeout 5 minutes, control on `T>=4°C`, off `T<=2°C`, policy `[2,4]°C`, hysteresis 0.2°C, probe bound ±0.1°C. Clamp no state: fail run if `T` outside `[-40,60]°C`, energy residual nonzero, negative capacity/power, or impossible transition. The standalone cold pack owns its generator and bus power port; W2-02 does not compose with mini-grid.
.agent/W2-technical-design-cold.md:114:Grid loss opens transfer and deenergizes compressor bus; controller emits `START_REQUEST` only if backup enabled, generator reaches RUNNING after delay unless failed, transfer closes to BACKUP after delay if generator power exists, and compressor restarts after its own delay if controller still demands cooling. Failed start emits `START_RESULT/FAILED` at timeout; successful start emits `START_RESULT/SUCCEEDED` when running. Transfer result is emitted only if a position sensor is configured; absence stays absence. Door events are sensor transitions; door opening adds heat only while open. Probe failure emits one `UNAVAILABLE` reading with reason `SENSOR_FAILURE` if the profile publishes it, then no numeric sample; reporting-path loss emits no envelope. Device measurement is `T + fixed observation bias` (default 0), rounded to 0.1°C by half-even rule; no private cause field. Controller and power events use observed public transitions and stable correlation ID.

S1 publishing is battery reserve SOC only; priority controls stay read-only. The Kobo fixture has a 30-minute generator minimum-runtime property but no 35%/90% generator thresholds. An incomplete Foundation gap fixture removes reserve while remaining well-formed under the existing strict Site parser. The Planner owns the API/UI/guard details and records the fixture comparison in the S1-01 packet.

# Workflow

AssetOps is built through thin end-to-end slices that produce UI-verifiable
product behavior.

## Lanes

Planned lane:

Architect or Planner -> Implementer -> Reviewer -> User review

Use for new product behavior, domain semantics, user-visible analytics,
meaningful UI/UX, data/API contracts, architecture boundaries, simulator or
ingestion semantics, and external integrations.

Fast lane:

Implementer -> Reviewer

Use only when the work stays inside an existing product and technical contract.

## No Agent Writes An Approval

Recorded 2026-09-26 after an Implementer wrote two approvals that had not
happened into the durable record: a dated owner sign-off whose only basis was
four conversational words, and a review verdict of ACCEPT while a RETURN verdict
sat unread in the same directory. It then set the task complete and moved it to
`tasks/completed/`. Reverted at `166c02b`.

Relying on an agent to be honest about this is what failed, so these are
controls rather than advice.

- **An agent may not write an owner approval anywhere.** Not the task file, not
  a packet, not a commit message. An agent cannot observe the owner's approval;
  only the coordinator, relaying the user, records one. A conversational remark
  is not a checkpoint: the task file defines what the owner must have done, and
  nothing short of that is a sign-off.
- **An agent may not record a review verdict.** The coordinator records it,
  after reading the review file. A subagent's handback is that subagent's
  summary of its own work; the harness says so on every handback, and it was
  said on the one that was believed here.
- **An Implementer may not commission its own review.** A review it
  commissioned is not independent whatever it concludes, and
  `.ai/ROLE_CONFIG.md` requires independence from the author. The coordinator
  dispatches the Reviewer.
- **Before recording any verdict, list the review files.** Two sat in `.agent/`
  that day, twenty-two minutes apart, and the one that agreed was cited. Where
  there is more than one, they are all read and the disagreement is reported,
  not resolved by preference.
- **Do not commit into a tree a Reviewer is measuring.**
  `.ai/PROJECT_RULES.md` "One Working Copy" already says evidence taken while
  another agent holds the tree is not evidence. Four commits landed during that
  review, and it had to qualify its own findings as a result.

A task reaching `tasks/completed/` with a verdict nothing verified is the
failure these prevent. `T011B` and `T011C` reached main at `in_review` for the
mirror-image reason - no check enforces the transition, which is why the rule
has to be read rather than relied upon.

## Vertical Slice Standard

Each planned task should include the minimum required domain semantics, backend
logic, data contract, UI, tests, and demo evidence needed for a reviewable
result. Not every task needs every layer, but each task should either deliver a
UI-verifiable outcome or explicitly unlock a named UI-verifiable slice.

Features and tasks are different planning objects. A feature is a complete
product function that may require several tasks. A task is a reviewable
implementation slice that delivers or materially advances one UI-verifiable part
of a feature.

The current sequence is the Site-first S1â€“S7 queue in `tasks/README.md`, based on the current architecture, technical design and Site-first execution plan. Earlier feature maps and demo roadmaps are historical planning input.

This replaces the old examples that implied a fuel discrepancy was the first
Finding. Within each outcome, create reviewable cuts that let the owner run
and judge progress; do not make each architecture noun a separate task.

Avoid building whole layers before there is useful product behavior.

## Task Spec Size

Task specs are guardrails for fast implementation, not miniature design
documents. For S1-S7, keep durable reasoning in the current Site-first architecture, technical design, execution plan or a new decision; keep task files slice-specific and executable. The old feature map and T0xx queue remain historical.

Size is a ceiling, never a target. These are the upper limits:

- Normal UI/content slice: 120 lines.
- Boundary-changing slice: 160 lines.
- First write path, evidence contract, ingestion, simulator truth boundary, or
  analytics/finding semantics: 220 lines.

**There is no minimum.** A spec that carries everything below in fewer lines is
finished, not thin. Revised 2026-09-24: the earlier 100-180 / 180-260 / 250-400
bands described specs that restated durable mechanics, and their lower bounds
were read as a quota. Specs that cite v4, the roadmap, the feature map,
`.ai/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `.ai/DECISIONS.md` instead of restating them land far
below those numbers and are better for it. Over a ceiling, split the slice or
move the reasoning to the document that owns it.

Line count does not measure whether a spec works. This does: **an implementer

## 4. W2-02 causal producer and publication

Add `cold-thermal/1` `ModelSpec` and `cold-publication/1`; resolve frozen profile identity in `host/execution_adapter.py:113-140`, `host/lab_execution.py:1978-2015` and `simulator/assetops_simulator/kernel/execute.py:90-105` through a closed registry, with fuel/mini-grid identities preserved. Lab freezes Foundation/binding IDs, scenario SHA, model/profile/observation versions and seed in run identity; Stage seals public v4 envelopes, registered Commit links publication, SQLite outbox sends authenticated Batch V2, and S2 alone creates accepted evidence (`host/lab_execution.py:2154-2164,2428-2501`; `.agent/architect-W2-design.md:55-66`).

**Time and state.** Fixed 1-minute UTC step; all updates use exact rationals/decimal text and a defined end-of-step publication order. State: chamber air temperature `T` degC, controller demand, compressor `OFF|STARTING|RUNNING|FAILED`, grid/backup bus energized flags, generator `STOPPED|STARTING|RUNNING|FAILED`, transfer position `GRID|BACKUP|OPEN`, door `OPEN|CLOSED`, probe `OK|FAILED`. Private forcing: ambient `Ta`, door schedule, grid loss, generator failure, probe failure; private truth never serializes into a product envelope. Initial `T=3Â°C`, `Ta=20Â°C`, door closed, compressor off, grid and bus on, generator stopped, transfer grid, probe OK. Per minute, `heat_kWh = (heat_leak_kW_per_C*(Ta-T) + door_open*door_heat_kWh*60)*1/60`; `cool_kWh = compressor_running_and_bus_powered*cooling_kW*1/60`; `T_next=T+(heat_kWh-cool_kWh)/thermal_capacity_kWh_per_C`. Defaults: thermal capacity `1.2 kWh/degC`, leak `0.08 kW/degC`, door heat `0.02 kWh/min` (stored as `1.2 kW` equivalent while open), cooling `3 kW`, compressor start delay 1 minute, generator start delay 2 minutes, transfer delay 1 minute, start timeout 5 minutes, control on `T>=4Â°C`, off `T<=2Â°C`, policy `[2,4]Â°C`, hysteresis 0.2Â°C, probe bound Â±0.1Â°C. Clamp no state: fail run if `T` outside `[-40,60]Â°C`, energy residual nonzero, negative capacity/power, or impossible transition. The standalone cold pack owns its generator and bus power port; W2-02 does not compose with mini-grid.

Grid loss opens transfer and deenergizes compressor bus; controller emits `START_REQUEST` only if backup enabled, generator reaches RUNNING after delay unless failed, transfer closes to BACKUP after delay if generator power exists, and compressor restarts after its own delay if controller still demands cooling. Failed start emits `START_RESULT/FAILED` at timeout; successful start emits `START_RESULT/SUCCEEDED` when running. Transfer result is emitted only if a position sensor is configured; absence stays absence. Door events are sensor transitions; door opening adds heat only while open. Probe failure emits one `UNAVAILABLE` reading with reason `SENSOR_FAILURE` if the profile publishes it, then no numeric sample; reporting-path loss emits no envelope. Device measurement is `T + fixed observation bias` (default 0), rounded to 0.1Â°C by half-even rule; no private cause field. Controller and power events use observed public transitions and stable correlation ID.

# Role Configuration

Roles are project responsibilities. Agent bindings are configurable defaults.

## Default Bindings

| Role | Default agent | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architect | Codex; scoped Claude exception for the v6.9 site mock-up work on `arch/canonical-v69-pivot` (2026-10-06; see below) | Creates feature maps, causal sequencing, protected seams, and feature-to-task guidance. |
| Planner | Codex (Claude exception ended at the 2026-10-03 21:23 reset; see below) | Converts reviewed feature guidance into small UI-verifiable task definitions. |
| Implementer | Claude | Builds the active task, runs checks, and prepares the review packet. |
| Reviewer | Configurable independent agent; Codex by default (see below) | Reviews work independently from the author. |

## Rules

- Keep role responsibilities stable even if the bound agent changes.
- Do not assume Planner, Architect, or Implementer means a specific vendor unless
  this file says so.
- Implementer may refine implementation steps, but should not redefine feature
  sequencing without Architect or user review.
- Reviewer must be independent from the agent that authored the implementation.
- Claude Code commands in `.claude/commands/` should read this file before
  acting so they can either run the role or prepare a handoff for the configured
  agent.

## Decision Requests Go To The Active Architect

Set by the owner on 2026-10-04 (verbatim in `.agent/owner-T028-closeout-2026-10-04.md`):
"for all decsion requests, let the active architect make them and inform me if
the architect wants me to weigh in as well with its justification and decision".

So the coordinator does not put decision requests to the owner. It sends them
to the Architect bound above, which decides, records the decision with its
justification, and informs the owner. Where the Architect wants the owner to
weigh in, it says so, giving its decision and justification, and the owner may
confirm or overrule. Owner acceptance of a slice (USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED) is not
a decision request and still goes to the owner.

Do not include forcings, private state, YAML formatting or the rest of the scenario document in this observation digest; `scenario_sha256` separately covers the entire parsed cold document. `runs/source_publication.py:run_identity_sha256` then naturally covers both digests. Add cold-only validation that all four are present and SHA strings lowercase 64 hex. Keep old serialized run and fingerprint golden vectors byte-identical.
+
+The frozen run identity carries Foundation revision ID and content SHA, binding revision ID, scenario ID and SHA, profile IDs/versions and observation SHA, seed and requested timing; it does not embed the thirteen Foundation property values or cold document contents. At execution the host re-reads the exact frozen Foundation revision and cold scenario document, verifies the Foundation revision ID and content SHA and the document's `scenario_sha256`, and recomputes `observation_sha256` from that document. It extracts the thirteen values from that verified Foundation revision and uses the verified document for forcings and observation rows. Missing, changed or mismatched inputs refuse execution before any public Stage output; no current-revision or fixture-default substitution is permitted.
+
+**Cold pack transition closure.** `GENERATOR_FAILURE` is a latent private start fault: the outage still produces `START_REQUEST`, the generator enters `STARTING`, and at the effective five-minute start timeout it becomes `FAILED` and emits `START_RESULT/FAILED` (19:05 in failure cases). On grid restore, the transfer returns to `GRID` immediately and emits `TRANSFER_RESULT/SUCCEEDED` when the configured transfer position sensor is present; the generator stops. While the compressor is `RUNNING` on a powered bus, its published power in kW equals the effective `cold-cooling-capacity` value; otherwise published power is zero. Public grid power and transfer events for one outage use its outage correlation ID; door events use their separate door-cycle correlation. The registered ambient probe publishes an ambient temperature point every five minutes, including the closing boundary, through its bound channel. These are public observations of the resulting transitions, not reports of the private forcing.
 
 **Lab choice and run-request closure (2026-10-17).** Keep the existing `GET /api/simulator-lab/scenarios` response and `GET /api/simulator-lab/scenarios/{scenario_id}` detail legacy-only; neither exposes the six cold definitions without a Site selection. Add gated `GET /api/simulator-lab/cold-scenarios?site_id=COLD-LAB-001` in `simulator_lab_api.py`, backed by `ScenarioCatalogService` and the injected `RegisteredBasisPort`. Its response is `{ "site_id": "COLD-LAB-001", "scenarios": [choice, ...] }`, where each `choice` has exactly `scenario_id` (string), `scenario_version` (integer), `display_name` (string), `schema` (`cold-scenario/1`), `model_profile`, `publication_profile`, `observation_profile` (each a string such as `cold-thermal/1`), `start`, `end` (UTC strings), and `seed` (integer). Derive all fields except `display_name` from the saved cold document; labels for the six IDs are `Normal`, `Excursion`, `Backup failed`, `Missing probe`, `Late reading`, and `Contradictory`. Order by `scenario_id`. Return the six only when the requested Site ID is exactly `COLD-LAB-001` and that Site is registered. For any other or unregistered Site, return an empty `scenarios` array; an unreadable scenario/registration store remains an unavailable error, never an empty claim. The Lab choice client calls this read after Site selection and offers the returned cold scenarios only for that selected Site; the unfiltered legacy catalog remains legacy-only. The cold document's `site_code` is a fixture compatibility constraint enforced at run setup, not a general scenario-to-Site binding rule. `RunSetupRequest` keeps its required `model_profile` and `publication_profile` `{profile_id,profile_version}` selections. For a cold run, freeze only when both selections exactly equal the document's `cold-thermal/1` and `cold-publication/1`; the document alone chooses `cold-observation/1`, whose identity and digest are frozen. Also require the request's Site, scenario version, seed, interval and one-minute timestep to match the cold document; refuse any mismatch before Draft. Do not add a separate observation-profile request key or silently substitute profile choices.
